gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-poly: Neon-tube lines, ruler straight. Bruno Ace draws every stroke at a single width, while Poly, a text serif, lets each bowl swell slightly like pressed glass, so the heading looks machined and the body looks softly handmade.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-quattrocento: Traditional at heart, Quattrocento is the text serif here, but Bruno Ace leads. Bruno Ace does its best work with flat, unvarying strokes that announce themselves; Quattrocento does its best with a mild thick-and-thin rhythm and daylight inside every curve.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-radley: Stencil-flat and sign-painter bold: that's Bruno Ace. Radley, a classic serif, then reads with a comfortable lean from sturdy downstrokes into slender turns, so paragraphs feel dignified and easy to settle into.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-roboto-serif: Roboto Serif has big open eyes and light contrast between verticals and curves. Bruno Ace is best at spaghetti-like strokes of one width that draw attention; Roboto Serif is best at spacing its letters generously and staying quiet.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-sahitya: Not one stroke of Bruno Ace swells or thins, just constant line from end to end. Sahitya, the classic serif, does its best work with restrained swells in the curves and open mouths on the s and c.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-sawarabi-mincho: Sawarabi Mincho brings a classic serif with moderate contrast and terminals cut well short of the bowl. And Bruno Ace sits above it as unshaded, constant strokes, so the heading feels drawn by ruler while the text feels refined.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-sedan: Sedan reads mellow, with fuller stems and slimmer links. Bruno Ace is best at curves that never thin at the shoulders and a lingering one-character-per-beat rhythm; Sedan, a text serif, is best at a soft, bookish cadence.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-sedan-sc: Stencil-cut letters of one steady width define Bruno Ace. And Sedan SC, a serif with broad open counters and a mild stress in the o and e, softens that rigid line into something literary.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-shippori-mincho: Shippori Mincho reads like hand-drawn ink, soft in its modulation. Bruno Ace adds a swell-free, ruler-drawn line up top, and the classic serif below keeps generous openings in every curve.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-shippori-mincho-b1: Refined and editorial, Shippori Mincho B1 has a crescent-wrench c and sturdy hairlines. And Bruno Ace is best at a rope-thin outline with no thick or thin parts, while the serif body is best at a modulation that never snags the eye.
